_comment: 🧩️ This subset's own contribution. `s.draw.draw` is a semio-NATIVE artifact carried in `.dsl.semio`/`.pack.semio`, so no third party can serve as its reference — see the noOracleDecision below. ONE catalog covers this subset's two declared 🧬️mutations directories: `🧬️schema/🧬️mutations` holds the `DrawMutation` enum, and `🚪️io/🧬️mutations` holds that SAME enum's text and binary wire codecs (`encode_op`/`decode_op`), not a second vocabulary — the completeness gate keys a catalog to the subset, and the subset has exactly one.

noOracleDecisions.rationale: No third-party crate reads or writes semio's `.dsl.semio`/`.pack.semio` envelope, and none is authoritative over `DrawMutation`. The vocabulary is not a generic tree-edit list either: it is derived from `DrawSnapshot`'s RECURSIVE layer tree, where a layer is one of several node kinds (group, path, trace, …) sharing a `base` record, so `update-layer-trace-params` exists only for the trace node kind while `set-layer-boolean-operation`, `replace-layer-fill` and `replace-layer-stroke` reach into the shared `attributes` record, and `create-layer`/`duplicate-layer`/`reorder-layer` address a PARENT plus an index rather than a flat position. Layer ids are content-addressed, which is why `create-layer` with an existing node is a hard rejection rather than a duplicate. Confidence comes from the committed per-kind specification vectors under `../🧬️schema/🧬️mutations/<kind>/🧪️tests/<fixture>/` — a `(before, mutation, after, diff, outcome)` quintet per kind, already unit-tested inside the production crate — plus the inverse law as a metamorphic property: applying a kind and then its own computed inverse must restore the exact pre-mutation document, POSITION in the tree included. The `mutate-draw-1` case re-exercises those SAME committed bytes end-to-end through `apply_draw_mutation`/`inverse_draw_mutation`, and crosses the real committed `Semio Emblem` drawing through both of its codecs for the identity law.
